title: What happened in AI — Nov 19, 2026
intro: The tool layer moved out of the prompt today. Gemini now loads tool schemas on demand, LangSmith put credentials and permissions behind a gateway, and Vercel shipped eve 1.0.
Security evidence cut both ways. An audit found AgentDojo scored 433 real attacks as misses, while an autonomous Codex run reported 507 Webmin bugs for about $4,578.
highlights: AgentDojo scored 433 runs as no attack even when the agent paid the attacker; re-check security claims built on it.
Gemini API Tool Retrieval (preview): set defer_loading and add tool_search to load tool schemas only when needed.
An autonomous Codex campaign reported 507 reproduced Webmin vulnerabilities for about $4,578 in tokens.
Vercel's eve agent framework reached 1.0; LangSmith Tool Gateway entered public beta for governed tool calls.
agent-framework follow-up: PyPI quarantined Microsoft's publisher; the attacker may still have publish access.
DeepSeek dropped separate fees for model-triggered search and web fetch.

categories.name: Tool layers: load less, govern more
categories.summary: Vendors moved tool handling out of the prompt: schemas load on demand, credentials sit behind a gateway, and output JSON gets compressed in a proxy.

articles.title: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
articles.summary: Preview in the Interactions API: add a tool_search tool with defer_loading true and Gemini fetches parameter schemas only when needed, cutting input tokens for large tool libraries.

articles.title: LangSmith Tool Gateway: Secure, governed tool use for agents
articles.summary: Public beta managed tool layer that holds credentials, decides which tools each agent may call and under whose identity, and logs every action.

articles.title: Show HN: Wiretuple – Cut LLM structured-output tokens with positional tuples
articles.summary: Zero-dependency Go reverse proxy that rewrites repeated JSON keys into positional tuples, claiming 35–60% fewer output tokens for structured outputs and function calls.

articles.title: Discovery: Fail-closed authority checks for AI agent tool calls (v1.0-v1.1.8)
articles.summary: Solo project that refuses tool calls when untrusted prompt text tries to mint authority or replay receipts; publishes 3,315/3,315 verified receipt hashes.

categories.name: Agent harnesses grow up: frameworks, state, sandboxes
categories.summary: Agent runtimes are becoming infrastructure with GA labels, in-house standards, and durable state, not per-team experiments.

articles.title: Eve 1.0 – Agent framework from Vercel
articles.summary: Vercel's open-source agent framework hits GA after 230+ preview releases, adding approval controls for actions and an eval suite for how well coding agents build with it.

articles.title: Aviator: HubSpot's Agent Harness
articles.summary: HubSpot explains why it built one internal agent harness in 2025 after teams kept making divergent model and architecture choices.

articles.title: Coordinated Snapshots of Agent State
articles.summary: Hatchet argues agent sandboxes need coordinated snapshots of state across processes, not just isolated compute.

articles.title: Docker AI Rebranded
articles.summary: Docker docs now lead with agent sandboxes: scheduled tasks run in a fresh cloud sandbox that is deleted when the task ends or times out.

articles.title: OSS Minymaton (event-driven MCP message bus for AI agents, bundled SQLite)
articles.summary: Durable, event-driven MCP message bus with bundled SQLite so several coding agents can hand off API changes and test failures without a human relaying them.

categories.name: Evals that check what the agent did
categories.summary: Today's eval work audits actions and traces instead of trusting a model's reply text or one automated verdict.

articles.title: Did the attack work? Auditing AI-agent security benchmark verdicts
articles.summary: Audit of AgentDojo: the benchmark scored 433 runs as no attack even though the agent paid the attacker or took another decisive action, 11.9% of real attacks. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Show HN: Agentest – offline tests for AI agents from OpenTelemetry traces
articles.summary: Open-source, offline suite of 165 deterministic tests over OpenTelemetry GenAI traces that flags unearned success claims, hidden-instruction follows, and forbidden tool calls with no LLM judge.

articles.title: LLM call is doing more than you think
articles.summary: Audiala swapped an LLM router for a decision model and rolled back in 23 minutes: the old call also resolved cities, references, and tool flags nobody evaluated.

articles.title: Genie One Accuracy: Why Curated Agents Need Governed Context
articles.summary: Databricks used 125 insurance questions to show agents need governed business definitions; Finance and Underwriting gave opposite, correct loss-ratio answers.

categories.name: Security: AI finds bugs, supply chain still leaks
categories.summary: Autonomous auditing got cheap enough to run on a whole codebase while package and model supply chains stayed the soft spot.

articles.title: Autonomous AI Security Auditing of Webmin: 507 Newly Discovered Vulnerabilities
articles.summary: A fully autonomous Codex campaign reported 507 reproduced vulnerabilities in Webmin 2.670 using 8.35B tokens, about US$4,578 at standard API rates.

articles.title: Official Microsoft agent-framework PyPI package compromised
articles.summary: Follow-up: PyPI quarantined the Microsoft publisher because the attacker is believed to still have publishing access; treat any 1.26.1 or 1.26.2 install as a credential compromise.

articles.title: Three breaches, endless leaks: Your AI supply chain needs canaries
articles.summary: Dragos argues for canary tokens across the AI supply chain so a leaked key or poisoned dependency trips an alarm when used.

categories.name: Agents doing production engineering work
categories.summary: Large operators described agents that run inside their own engineering loops, from performance fixes to RL rollouts.

articles.title: How OpenAI’s Performance Factory keeps ChatGPT fast
articles.summary: OpenAI runs Codex-powered workflows that find and fix performance regressions to keep ChatGPT fast.

articles.title: How Meta Uses AI Agents to Scale ML Innovations Across Ads Ranking Models
articles.summary: Meta uses agents to port proven ranking techniques across its many ads models, each with different architecture, data, and serving limits.

articles.title: How Abundant designed efficient rollout architecture with Modal Sandboxes
articles.summary: Abundant runs RL rollouts for frontier labs on Modal Sandboxes, giving each task its own isolated environment, Dockerfile, and verifier.

categories.name: Token prices and compute deals
categories.summary: Chinese and Indian labs competed on price while compute commitments shifted in both directions.

articles.title: DeepSeek Removes Separate Fees for Model-Triggered Search and Web Fetch
articles.summary: DeepSeek no longer charges separately when the model triggers search or web fetch, which simplifies cost math for tool-using agents.

articles.title: Sarvam Prices Its Own Model Below DeepSeek In New Token Factory
articles.summary: Sarvam's new token factory lists its own model below DeepSeek's price.

articles.title: Moonshot AI Cancels $150 Million Nvidia B300 GPU Rental Deal in Indonesia
articles.summary: Moonshot AI cancelled a $150 million Nvidia B300 GPU rental deal in Indonesia.

articles.title: NVIDIA and Microsoft Expand Accelerated Computing From Azure to Windows PCs
articles.summary: At Ignite, Microsoft widens access to Azure VMs on NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and extends the stack to Windows PCs.
